_doc: Which evaluation METRIC MODELS cover which languages. Transcribed cite-only from each model's own published list, with the URL and the date read — the same discipline as method-coverage.json. This exists because the harness selects a specialised COMET model per language, and the previous source for that was two hardcoded ISO lists inside a script, one of which cited the wrong paper on all 109 cards it touched.
_boundary: This is RESOURCE EXISTENCE — that a metric model claims to cover a language. It is never a score, and never a claim about how well anything evaluates. A measured metric value is a run result keyed by (method, dataset, metric) and belongs on the leaderboard.

models.label: AfriCOMET-MTL
models.purpose: reference-based MT evaluation for African languages
models.citation: Wang et al. AfriMTE and AfriCOMET: Empowering COMET to Embrace Under-resourced African Languages. arXiv:2311.09828.
models.citationNote: The previous corpus cited this as 'wan-2022' on all 109 cards carrying the field. The model card names arXiv:2311.09828; the work was subsequently published at NAACL 2024, so both a 2023 (preprint) and 2024 (proceedings) year are defensible and the arXiv identifier is the unambiguous reference.
models.coverageStatement: This model builds on top of AfroXLMR which cover the following languages: [...]. Thus, results for language pairs containing uncovered languages are unreliable!
models.isoMappingNote: The publisher lists NAMES, not codes. The ISO 639-3 mapping below is OURS and is marked as such — it is a standard, checkable correspondence, but it is our step and not the publisher's. Four of the twenty resolve to MACROLANGUAGES (ara, mlg, orm, swa); whether coverage of a macrolanguage extends to its individual members is the same open question the atlas records for method coverage, and it is not answered here.
models.pivotNote: eng and fra appear in the publisher's language list as the evaluation PIVOTS its African-language pairs run through, not as African targets. Membership stays faithful to the publisher; the pivot marking is what keeps 'has AfriCOMET' meaning what the model is FOR — recommending africomet-mtl for French because French is a pivot would route a high-resource language away from the default COMET its own validation covers.
models.qeNote: Reference-free QE sibling (AfriCOMET-QE-STL), same publisher, same language list, same citation — relocated from the per-card `qe` variant every legacy card stamped with africomet-wan-2022.

models.label: XLM-R top-tier training languages
models.purpose: COMET reliability signal: languages with high XLM-R representation produce more reliable COMET scores
models.citation: Conneau et al. 2020, Unsupervised Cross-lingual Representation Learning at Scale (XLM-R) — top-100 languages by CommonCrawl training volume
models.tierMeaning: membership in this list IS the 'high' tier; the paper publishes the list, not per-language scores
models.relocationNote: 2026-08-11: transcribed cite-only onto cards long ago (source stamp 'xlmr-conneau-2020' on every entry) and relocated here, the register such transcriptions belong in — the same move as DeepL formality.

xlmr.whatItWasFor: arena/mt_eval_harness/language_cards.py::is_xlmr_high_resource, read by metrics_comet.py and metrics_metricx.py to flag a score as potentially noisy because the underlying embeddings are weak for that language.
xlmr.published: XLM-RoBERTa's model card states it was pre-trained on 'filtered CommonCrawl data containing 100 languages' (Conneau et al., arXiv:1911.02116). Checked 2026-08-05.
xlmr.whyUnresolved: The model card gives the COUNT and not the LIST. The 100 language codes are in the paper's appendix, which is not a source that can be fetched and pinned the way a model card can. Transcribing them by hand is exactly how the previous register acquired a 'Top-100' note over a list of 77.
xlmr.failSafe: Until the list is pinned, is_xlmr_high_resource returns False for every language, so every score carries the low-resource caveat. That OVER-warns rather than under-warns, which is the only safe direction for a reliability flag: a caveat on a reliable score costs a reader nothing, and a missing caveat on an unreliable one costs them their conclusion.
xlmr.theFix: A fetcher against a citable enumeration of CC-100 / XLM-R's language set, pinned like any other source.
